kind.description: paper: a published or preprint work, durable and re-checkable. observation: something the catalog's owner personally noticed. post: informal public writing -- a thread, a blog entry, a forum comment. A post can originate a claim but cannot strongly back one; it caps at own-observation backing, and never counts as replicated.

content_url.description: Direct link to the exact file read, where that differs from `url`. For a paper maintained in a repository this is the raw file, which is the canonical copy.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file at content_url when it was read. Pins which version a claim rests on. Papers on arXiv get a version in their id; a PDF served from a repo can change under the same URL with nothing to notice it.

content_checked_at.description: When content_sha256 was last confirmed to still match.

content_changed_at.description: Set when the file at content_url stopped matching content_sha256. Claims citing this source need re-reading; the figures they quote may have been revised.

author_handle.description: For kind: post — the author's handle or username, e.g. "@cherylwoooo".

retrieved_at.description: For kind: post — when the text below was captured. Required with archived_text.

archived_text.description: For kind: post — the post's text, verbatim, captured at retrieved_at. REQUIRED for kind: post. Posts are deleted and edited; a paper can be re-fetched years later and a post cannot. Without the archive the citation quietly stops being checkable, which is worse than not having it.

brief.description: A reader-facing digest of the paper in the house summary style (docs/prompts/paper-summary.md): finding first, method, figures, boundary, takeaway. Generated from the abstract by scripts/summarize-sources.mjs and number-checked against it. Distinct from `summary`, which is a one-or-two-sentence factual gloss written by hand.

brief_source.description: What the brief was written from. Full text is available only for papers arXiv renders as HTML (roughly Dec 2023 onward); everything older falls back to the abstract, and its figures and evidence-quality paragraph are correspondingly thinner.

brief_unverified_figures.description: Numbers that appear in `brief` but not in the source abstract it was generated from. Should normally be empty; a non-empty list means the digest needs a human read before it is trusted.
